knowledgePattern: Combine side positivity with the strict two-triangle SSA conditions

hints.title: Check that both sides are positive
hints.body: Factor or rearrange each side length and determine the interval on which both are genuine positive lengths.
hints.recap: Sign restrictions must be established before cancelling a variable factor from inequalities.
hints.pitfall: An algebraic length may be zero or negative outside the geometric domain.

recall.reminder: Sign restrictions must be established before cancelling a variable factor from inequalities.

hints.title: Locate the perpendicular height
hints.body: Draw the perpendicular from C to the ray through A. Compare the opposite side with that height and with AC to decide when the ray is met twice.
hints.recap: For an acute SSA configuration, the height and adjacent side determine how many nondegenerate triangles are possible.
hints.pitfall: Equality can merge the two triangles or create a zero-length side.
hints.pause: Translate the two-triangle condition into strict inequalities in x and solve them.

recall.reminder: For an acute SSA configuration, the height and adjacent side determine how many nondegenerate triangles are possible.

solution:
1. Write a=BC=(x−3)(x−2) and b=AC=(x−3)(8−x). The condition b>0 gives 3<x<8, and a is positive throughout this interval.

2. The perpendicular distance from C to the ray making 30∘ at A is bsin30∘=b/2. Two distinct intersections on that ray require the opposite side a to be greater than this height but less than b: b/2<a<b.

3. Since x−3>0, cancel it without reversing signs. The inequalities become (8−x)/2<x−2<8−x. They give x>4 and x<5.

4. Combining all conditions gives 4<x<5. At 4 the intersections merge; at 5 one intersection is A and the triangle is degenerate. Answer D.
